title: CRB-65 score pour pneumonie gravité
formula:
The CRB-65 Score is calculated by the addition of the selected points:

| Variable | Points | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C onfusion | No | 0 |
| Yes | 1 | |
| R espiratory rate ≥ 30/min | No | 0 |
| Yes | 1 | |
| B lood pressure (SBP <90 mm Hg or DBP ≤60 mm Hg) | No | 0 |
| Yes | 1 | |
| Age ≥65 | No | 0 |
| Yes | 1 | |

how_to_use.why:
- Grades CAP severity by estimating 30-day mortality, guiding disposition decisions (outpatient vs. inpatient).
- A quick and simple calculation that requires no laboratory data, which can be ideal for resource-limited settings or where immediate laboratory results are not available.
- Endorsed by multiple organizations, including the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) and the American Academy of Family Physicians (AAFP).
how_to_use.when:
- Use to assess adult patients with suspected or confirmed community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) in primary care, urgent-care, or other pre-hospital settings.
- Especially useful when laboratory data are not yet available.
how_to_use.pearls:
- Derived from the British Thoracic Society (BTS) [CURB-65 model](nabda:calc.curb-65-score-pneumonia-severity) ; CRB-65 omits the urea criterion, relying solely on clinical findings while preserving comparable prognostic accuracy.
- Does not capture all predictors of CAP severity, such as nursing home residency, recent hospitalization, or recent antibiotics; incorporate these factors into the overall assessment.
- [McNally et al. (2010)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20883616/)found that the tool may overestimate 30-day mortality in community cohorts, particularly in the intermediate-risk group.

next_steps.advice:
- Interpret the score alongside a thorough clinical evaluation; low scores do not override red flags such as hypoxemia, multilobar infiltrates, severe comorbidities, immunosuppression, or poor social support.
- Use the tool primarily for disposition; antimicrobial choice, fluids, labs, cultures, and imaging should follow guideline-based best practice and clinical judgment.
- Although CAP can be viral, empiric antibiotics are usually prescribed to cover potential bacterial pathogens.
next_steps.critical_actions: Be sure to screen for other signs of sepsis and initiate appropriate management bundles; helpful tools may include (but are not limited to) [SIRS](nabda:calc.sirs-sepsis-septic-shock-criteria) , [NEWS](nabda:calc.national-early-warning-score-news) , [SOFA](nabda:calc.sequential-organ-failure-assessment-sofa-score) / [qSOFA](nabda:calc.qsofa-quick-sofa-score-sepsis) .
next_steps.management:
- **Low risk (score 0):** Outpatient care with timely follow-up and clear return precautions.
- **Moderate risk (score 1–2):** Same-day hospital assessment; consider admission or short-stay/observation.
- **High risk (score ≥3):** Urgent hospital admission and early intensive-care evaluation.

more_info:
Interpretation:

| CRB-65 Score | Mortality Risk | Treatment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Low | Likely suitable for home treatment |
| 1 or 2 | Intermediate | Consider hospital referral |
| 3 or 4 | High | Urgent hospital admission |
